newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia seen set for tourism boost in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatia seen set for tourism boost in 1997.

text.p: Croatia expects a 20 percent rise in the number of tourist overnights, and 30 to 40 percent better financial results in the coming tourist season, Tourism Minister Niko Bulic was quoted as saying on Thursday.

The 1996 tourist season was the first successful season after years of recession and slow growth due to the war fought in Croatia and neighbouring Bosnia. The tourist industry is seen as the main engine of the economy.
Bulic predicted the number of overnights to rise to over 26.5 million in 1997 from just under 22 million last year, in an interview for Zagreb daily Vecernj List.
Financial results should be even better, with the total tourist spending estimated at 13 to 14 billion kuna in comparison with under 10 billion last year, Bulic said.

"The 20-percent growth should reflect favourably on the entire economy," Bulic said in a pre-election interview. He is running as a ruling party candidate in Dubrovnik county in the municipal elections set for next Sunday.

Bulic said the country is much better prepared for receiving tourists than it was last year, especially in terms of newly-built infrastructure, refurbished hotels, tidied up tourist resorts and border crossings.
